title: Async allocator staleness and cache residue causing long-tail memory growth
creator: Samira Patel
description: Summary: We observe progressive GPU resident memory growth during high-throughput continuous batching workloads that do heavy KV cache prefetching. The growth survives multiple request windows and only partially reclaims after long idle periods. Symptoms look unlike a simple allocation leak; instead it appears related to cudaMallocAsync staging/pool churn combined with many short-lived pinned staging buffers from the KV prefetch pipeline. This ticket coordinates the root-cause investigation and tracks experiments to mitigate long-tail memory retention and fragmentation.
reproduction_steps:
1) Deploy runtime-1.22 build with KV prefetch enabled (prefetch_window=4) on p4d instance.
2) Load test with steady stream: median seq_len=1024, batch_size=12, continuous arrival at ~250 rps for 90 minutes.
3) Monitor nvidia-smi, cuda memory pool stats (CU_MEMPOOL API), and allocator internal metrics.
4) Observe resident memory and fragmentation metrics every 5 minutes.
investigation_notes:
- Initial observation: resident GPU memory increases ~30-45 MB/min in the first 30 minutes, then rate slows but never returns to baseline after stopping traffic.
- Heap maps: many allocations in 'staging' stream (stream 2) show deferred frees logged by cudaMallocAsync until stream synchronization points.
- KV prefetch path creates ~3k short-lived pinned host staging buffers per minute at this workload. These are being promoted into the async pool and held as 'resident arenas' due to pool hysteresis thresholds.
- Fragmentation metric (free_chunks > 512 bytes) increased by 18% across slabs after 2 hours.
- Turning off prefetch reduces the long-tail growth but increases tail latency for cold requests.
- Observed swap behavior: when host pinned staging is high, fallback to pinned host allocations causes host GPU driver pressure and sporadic allocation failures under heavy load.
experiments_tried: A: Toggle CUDA_MALLOC_ASYNC=0 at runtime: immediate drop in long-tail growth but 6% worse median latency for cold-prefix requests.
B: Reduce pool max_resident_bytes by 30% via env override: reduced resident plateau but increased allocation churn and slight kernel launch variance.
C: Serializing prefetch stream (single stream instead of per-request streams): reduced deferred free backlog by 40% but increased blocking on IO for some clients.
D: Pre-alloc slab of KV-prefetch buffers sized to 2x measured working set: eliminated frequent allocations but increased baseline resident by ~1.5GB and did not reduce fragmentation over long runs.
findings_summary: Root causes appear to be a combination of: (1) many short-lived pinned staging allocations from KV prefetch that get funneled into cudaMallocAsync pools; (2) pool hysteresis and asynchronous free semantics delaying reclamation; and (3) allocator slab sizing that mismatches observed sequence-length/batch-size distribution leading to internal fragmentation. The issue is not a classic unreachable pointer leak but retention and fragmentation within the async pooling layer aggravated by high prefetch concurrency.
proposed_mitigations: Short term: Add an opt-in env flag RUNTIME_KV_PREFETCH_POOL_TTL_MS to aggressively trim staging arenas after N ms of inactivity (experimentally 120000 ms).
Short term: Introduce prefetch batching coalescing to reduce number of staging allocations per second (group small prefetches into shared buffers).
Mid term: Implement a pool compaction pass that attempts to cudaFree unused arenas during low load windows (throttled to avoid spikes).
Mid term: Tune default cudaMallocAsync pool sizing logic to account for sequence-length percentiles rather than a simple max request size heuristic.
Long term: Add per-tenant KV cache memory caps and eviction hooks that proactively release staging buffers that are orphaned from active KV windows.
Operational: Surface a 'pool residency' metric in Console with alerting when async pool grows > 80% of device memory for > 10 minutes.
acceptance_criteria: Repro test: Under the same traffic profile, resident memory plateau is reduced by >=40% vs baseline (without disabling prefetch).
Regression: Median and P95 latency for cold-prefix requests must not regress by >5% after mitigations are enabled.
Monitoring: Console shows pool residency metric and an alert template created and wired to oncall playbook.
Rollout: Feature flags for TTL and coalescing implemented and tested in canary before ramp to production.
